text:
Ava (PM): quick sync — need alignment on the launch slice. customer pilot wants predictable latency and tenant isolation but we can't hit both without extra weeks. thoughts?
Rajat (Eng): emb cache and request coalescing are the big levers. removing prefix KV cache from MVP drops infra work by ~2w but ups per-token latency ~20-30ms.
Maya (ML PM): model quant + smaller context helped perf in perf-tests, but quality regressions show up for long instructions. we should keep a short set of golden prompts for evals if we drop cache.
Sam (UX): product experience-wise we can hide perf differences behind loading states for >200ms paths. main UX risk is multi-tenant join flow (SSO) — that is visible.
Dina (Sales): for the pilot, ACME said SSO is a 'must' for production, but they'd accept trial without it. their go/no-go is operator-level isolation and SLA.
Liam (Eng Manager): bandwidth out of infra team is the constraint. two realistic options: A) remove KV cache for MVP, keep single-region hosted, ship on-time; B) keep cache, push launch +3w.
Priya (CTO): tradeoff framing: do we compress scope or shift timeline? prefer compression if it doesn't create 2x operational cost later. also want a clear rollback/fallback plan.
Ava (PM): proposal: go with Option A (compress) but add strict gating: canary at 10% traffic, 72h health window, golden prompts perf within 15% of baseline. if fail -> hold and trigger plan B.
Rajat (Eng): can implement canary and a runtime flag to re-enable cache later. deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled by request.
Ava (PM): updated launch criteria (short): 1) <5% error rate at 10% canary, 2) golden prompt latency within 15% baseline, 3) telemetry and cost dashboard live, 4) rollback doc linked.
Sam (UX): I'll strip non-essential onboarding screens so we don't block backend. gives ~3 days dev buffer.
Maya (ML PM): I'll finalize the eval set and run overnight regressions against quant/uncached path. will post results here by EOD.
Dina (Sales): I'll tell ACME we can pilot without SSO but will commit to SSO in v1-ish timeline; ask them to sign pilot agreement.
Liam (Eng Manager): re: capacity — we can absorb 10% canary in-hosted pool; need ops oncall for 72h. scheduling now.
Priya (CTO): fine, but if the canary shows any model quality drift we revert before wide rollout. no partial rollouts without sign-off.
Ava (PM): next steps: (1) Rajat & Liam to wire runtime flag + canary (ETA 3 days), (2) Maya to post evals (EOD), (3) Sam to deliver trimmed flows (T+2d), (4) Dina to confirm pilot agreement (T+1d). I'll reconvene midday tomorrow.
Rajat (Eng): ack. I'll post a short runbook snippet here for rollback.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary window placeholder created: canary-id=c-1933333333-01, default 10% traffic, 72h TTL.
Ava (PM): thanks — keeping scope tight but having a fallback feels safer than slipping the date. if anything changes ping this thread and we'll escalate. :thumbsup:
